revisionPurpose: Reframe the first synthesis as accumulated SCZN3 shooting knowledge under the Founder-approved learning philosophy.

knowledgePhilosophy.expressionRule: Learn the knowledge; do not copy the expression.
knowledgePhilosophy.deliveryStandard: SCZN3 always tells the truth to its audience.

doesNotByItselfEstablish: universal truth for every shooter and context

coreModel: Define the shooter's objective, observe repeatable evidence, apply the best relevant knowledge SCZN3 has synthesized, make one useful change, compare the result, and learn from what happens next.
whatSczn3NowKnows: Begin with the shooter's objective rather than the target catalog.
Make the task, aim, response, and success condition clear.
Collect enough repeatable evidence to distinguish an event from a pattern.
Keep location, dispersion, timing, score, and sequence separate until a useful method combines them.
Compare like with like, change one useful variable, and confirm with new evidence.
Treat drills, diagnostics, courses, games, and progressions as different learning structures.
Preserve ambiguity when more than one explanation fits.
Preserve prior results so improvement can be learned over time.
commonizationGains: Sight-in products commonized into a zeroing and confirmation model.
Reactive paper, thermal marks, clean holes, contrast, and steel feedback commonized into visibility as an evidence concept.
Multiple aim points and replacement centers commonized into isolation of repetitions and clean comparison.
Diagnostic charts commonized into pattern evidence, context, ambiguity, and useful next action.
Slow, timed, rapid, time-factor, and penalty products commonized into separate accuracy and time facts joined only by an explicit method.
Competition and qualification products commonized into distinct target-face, course, practice-result, and official-outcome concepts.
Sequences and preserved histories commonized into distinct next-stage, readiness, and longitudinal-improvement concepts.
Games, cues, and scenarios commonized into attention, selection, sequence, state, and feedback concepts.
uncertainties: trigger, grip, wrist, anticipation, and follow-through guidance
rifle positional skill and load development
competition preparation beyond target and course execution
correction selection when shooter and equipment causes overlap
missingKnowledge: comprehensive shotgun fundamentals and pattern interpretation
movement, transitions, drawing, reloads, malfunction work, and use of cover
wind, field conditions, external ballistics, and positional rifle coaching

legal, tactical, medical, and use-of-force doctrine

domains.name: Fundamentals
domains.synthesis: Use a repeatable process spanning body position, grip, breath control, sight alignment, deliberate trigger operation, and follow-through; judge repeatability from a body of evidence rather than a slogan or isolated hole.
domains.limits: No single universal technique is established across all firearms and contexts.

domains.name: Accuracy and grouping
domains.synthesis: A single impact establishes location; a repeatable group provides stronger evidence of center, dispersion, bias, consistency, and outliers. Use clean aim areas and compare fresh groups after one controlled change.
domains.limits: A group location does not by itself prove a shooter cause or require an equipment correction.

domains.name: Sight and optic use
domains.synthesis: High-contrast references, grids, thermal signatures, known dimensions, range, and sight units make the aiming relationship measurable; corrections require compatible scale, units, and a valid correction model.
domains.limits: Reduced faces do not reproduce all full-distance ballistics or conditions.

domains.name: Trigger operation
domains.synthesis: Abrupt or inconsistent trigger operation may disturb the sighting relationship; evaluate it across enough group evidence, relevant context, and honest ambiguity conditions.
domains.limits: Do not infer a trigger diagnosis from one impact.

domains.name: Grip and control
domains.synthesis: Grip pressure, thumb/heel input, over-gripping, and wrist consistency can affect group location; handedness and exact target profile matter.
domains.limits: Never infer left-handed treatment by mirroring right-handed data.

domains.name: Zeroing
domains.synthesis: Declare aim, fire a repeatable group, measure center relative to aim, calculate only from compatible target/distance/sight units and a valid model, adjust, and confirm with a fresh group while preserving setup and load facts.
domains.limits: A sight-in label alone does not supply every measurement or correction rule.

domains.name: Diagnosing shot and group patterns
domains.synthesis: Compare an adequate evidence pattern with the best relevant diagnostic knowledge, present the supported interpretation and useful next action, and preserve unmatched, ambiguous, or no-reliable-conclusion outcomes.
domains.limits: The corpus lacks complete minimum-shot, confidence, mixed-pattern, and empirical validation rules.

domains.name: Recoil management
domains.synthesis: Anticipation, wrist behavior, grip, and follow-through are evidenced as relevant diagnostic concepts.
domains.limits: No comprehensive cross-platform recoil curriculum or progression is established.

domains.name: Speed versus accuracy
domains.synthesis: Define the acceptable response and exact timed interval, preserve accuracy and time separately, and combine them only through an explicit method.
domains.limits: No universal speed threshold or progression is established.

domains.name: Drills and repetition
domains.synthesis: A complete drill defines start, cue, intended response, repetitions or shot count, sequence, distance, timing policy, and terminal state. Multiple aim points aid repetition but do not create a drill by themselves.
domains.limits: Selectable artwork is drill potential until a versioned rule exists.

domains.name: Progression
domains.synthesis: Keep ordinal sequence, evidence of readiness, and longitudinal improvement separate. A publisher may establish what comes next without establishing that the shooter is ready.
domains.limits: The Baker guide and Thompson advancement criteria remain incomplete; reliable longitudinal delivery also needs continuous shooter identity.

domains.name: Pistol knowledge
domains.synthesis: The corpus supports pistol group evaluation, publisher-authored trigger/grip diagnostics, short-range cue work, formal slow/timed/rapid scoring, practice courses, and an ordinal training sequence.
domains.limits: Movement, draw, reload, malfunction work, fit, and validated coaching logic are thin or absent.

domains.name: Rifle knowledge
domains.synthesis: Rifle knowledge is strongest in sight-in, distance-specific and reduced faces, formal scoring, load records, zeroing, and defined course structures.
domains.limits: Position coaching, natural point of aim, sling, wind, transitions, external ballistics, and field shooting remain thin.

domains.name: Shotgun knowledge
domains.synthesis: Shotgun compatibility, turkey imagery, qualification references, and limited patterning intent are present.
domains.limits: Pattern density, POA/POI, choke/load comparison, fit, leads, moving targets, and purpose-specific acceptance criteria are not adequately established.

domains.name: Competition preparation
domains.synthesis: Exact face, regions, stages, allocation, penalties, timing, and practice results can be evaluated when the current rules are known; printer identity remains separate from the standardized target specification.
domains.limits: Target practice alone does not reproduce match administration, commands, equipment rules, or conditions.

domains.name: Qualification preparation
domains.synthesis: Keep evidence-only, practice/simulation evaluation, and official qualification distinct. Official claims require the course plus administration, identity, witness/instructor, facility, record, reporting, and credential requirements as applicable.
domains.limits: Many product labels lack current complete course definitions and official-program requirements.

domains.name: Beginner knowledge
domains.synthesis: Use clear tasks, visible impacts, uncomplicated aim references, clean repetition, and immediate review; vary aim size and distance with the shooter and objective.
domains.limits: The corpus lacks a comprehensive beginner safety, fit, and escalation curriculum.

domains.name: Common problems and corrective actions
domains.synthesis: Before correcting the shooter, distinguish insufficient evidence, measurement failure, task mismatch, equipment state, displaced coherent group, dispersion, and context-sensitive diagnostic patterns.
domains.limits: Advice must match the shooter objective, firearm, conditions, and evidence strength, and must permit no reliable conclusion.

domains.name: Feedback visibility
domains.synthesis: Reactive marks, high contrast, thermal signatures, clean holes, and steel movement or sound reduce the delay and effort required to observe results.
domains.limits: Visibility is an evidence affordance, not diagnosis or proof of improvement.

domains.name: Historical comparison
domains.synthesis: Improvement claims require comparable setup facts, exact source identity, preserved results, and immutable history; do not silently rescore old evidence.
domains.limits: Longitudinal comparison requires reliable shooter continuity and comparable conditions.

reconciliations.tension: large or reactive aim versus small precision aim
reconciliations.resolution: They serve different visibility, distance, and precision goals.
One impact records an event; a group provides stronger evidence of repeatability and bias.
They are separate facts until an exact rule combines them.
Treat each chart as an input, require enough evidence and relevant context, and preserve unmatched or ambiguous results.
Angular representation does not recreate every ballistic or environmental condition.
The face, course, and official administration are distinct authorities.
